title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setup. Let Π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = ⟨l_0, l_1, l_∞ | l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1⟩, with l_i a loop around the puncture i. The page studies how this group sits inside a small diagram of covers and quotients.

(1) The double cover. Grothendieck defines a character Π_{0,3} → {±1} by l_0, l_∞ ↦ −1 and l_1 ↦ +1. Its kernel π' corresponds to the double cover z ↦ z² branched over 0 and ∞. The cover is P^1 minus the preimages of the three punctures:
- 0 and ∞ (each ramified);
- the two preimages ±1 of 1.
So π' ≅ π_1(P^1−{0,±1,∞}), which is Π_{0,4}, free of rank 3. He gives generators: λ_{1/2} = l_0², λ_∞ = l_∞², λ_1 = l_1 and λ_0 = int(l_0^{-1}) l_1 = l_0^{-1} l_1 l_0. These are standard Reidemeister–Schreier generators, with λ_1 and λ_0 the loops around the two preimages of 1.

(2) Filling in a puncture. He then maps π' → Π_{0,3} by λ_0 ↦ l_0, λ_{1/2} ↦ 1, λ_1 ↦ l_1, λ_∞ ↦ l_∞. Killing λ_{1/2} = l_0² fills in the ramified point over 0. The result is P^1−{1,−1,∞}, again a thrice-punctured sphere; its loops are relabelled l_0, l_1, l_∞.

(3) The comparison diagram. The deck involution of z ↦ z² is z ↦ −z. It acts on P^1−{±1,∞}, and he calls this involution σ_∞. This gives the bottom row 1 → Π_{0,3} → Π_{0,3}·{1,σ_∞} → {±1} → 1. Here Π_{0,3}·{1,σ_∞} is the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient P^1−{1,∞} with an order-2 cone point at 0. That group is Π_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_0²⟩⟩. So the middle vertical map is the epimorphism φ: l_0 ↦ σ_∞, l_1 ↦ l_1, l_∞ ↦ ε_∞. This is the map that kills l_0², consistent with λ_{1/2} = l_0² ↦ 1. The '?' marks show he is still checking well-definedness.

(4) The check inside PSL_2(Z). He writes ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, ε_1 = ρσ_∞ and ε_∞ = ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ^{-1}, where σ_∞ has order 2 and ρ order 3. This is PSL_2(Z) = ⟨σ, ρ | σ², ρ³⟩, with the ε_i the three parabolic generators (product 1). Their squares generate Γ(2)/±1 ≅ Π_{0,3}, so l_i = ε_i². Then Π_{0,3}·{1,σ_∞} is the index-3 theta group ⟨S, T²⟩: one elliptic point of order 2 and two cusps.
- Well-definedness of φ requires the image of l_0 l_1 l_∞ to be 1, i.e. σ_∞ · ε_1² · ε_∞ = 1. This is the line 'ε_∞ l_1 σ_∞ = ε_∞ ε_1² σ_∞' up to cyclic order.
- The crossed-out line expands ρ^{-1}σρ^{-1}·ρσ·ρσ·σ = ρ^{-1}σσρ·σσ to σ_∞σ_∞ = 1, using σ² = 1.
- So φ is a well-defined epimorphism.

Purpose. The page explicitly describes the index-2/index-3 relations among Γ(2), the theta group and PSL_2(Z), read as maps between Π_{0,3}, Π_{0,4} and orbifold quotients. These relations involve the double cover z ↦ z², the involution z ↦ −z, and filling a puncture. They are the basic morphisms of the genus-0 'Teichmüller tower' through which Gal(Q̄/Q) / GT acts, and they yield 'quadratic' relations of the kind later studied for P^1−{0,±1,∞}.
errors: No real error. The conventions (which point is labelled 1/2, the cyclic order of the product relation) are not stated, so 'ε_∞ l_1 σ_∞' should be read as the relation l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1 up to cyclic permutation.
The '?' after l_0 ↦ σ_∞ and next to the boxed φ shows well-definedness was still being checked on the page. The subsequent computation settles it, provided σ_∞² = 1 and l_1 = ε_1².

ideas.what: Index-2 subgroup of Π_{0,3} given by the double cover z ↦ z² branched at 0, ∞; identification with π_1(P^1−{0,±1,∞}) via explicit Reidemeister–Schreier generators
ideas.modern_name: Π_{0,4} as kernel of a character of Π_{0,3}; cyclotomic (N=2) level structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used in GT context by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps; cyclotomic GT by Enriquez
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the genus-0 Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal on it, but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Filling in a puncture (λ_{1/2} = l_0² ↦ 1) to map Π_{0,4} back onto Π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: puncture-forgetting morphism in the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), tower of Teichmüller groupoids

ideas.what: Orbifold quotient by the involution z ↦ −z, giving Π_{0,3}·{1,σ_∞} = Π_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_0²⟩⟩, realised via σ (order 2) and ρ (order 3) as the theta group inside PSL_2(Z) with l_i = ε_i²
ideas.modern_name: theta group Γ_θ ⊃ Γ(2), PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2) ≅ S_3; S_3-symmetry of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); in GT context Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the S_3 symmetry and the modular group in connection with the tower

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard working computation: the Γ(2) ⊂ Γ_θ ⊂ PSL_2(Z) relations as morphisms in the genus-0 tower via z ↦ z². It is of historical interest as a trace of Grothendieck testing quadratic/dihedral symmetries in 1981-82, before Drinfeld's GT and the later N=2 cyclotomic work. However, the mathematics itself is classical and this exact link was later made explicitly in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'λ_0 = int(l_0^{-1}) l_1' means the inner automorphism by l_0^{-1} applied to l_1, i.e. l_0^{-1} l_1 l_0, as written in the second occurrence.
'engendré par' is written as a heading over the list of generators λ_0, λ_{1/2}, λ_1, λ_∞ of π'.
The vertical arrow labelled 'épi' is on the left map π' → Π_{0,3}.
The crossed-out last line reads ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ^{-1}·ρσ_∞·ρσ_∞·σ_∞, simplifying to σ_∞σ_∞. It verifies ε_∞ ε_1² σ_∞ = 1.
